deepdive.sec: Branded Jewellery / Jewellery Exports (US-centric) — Consumer Discretionary

bull_bear.body:
- **Dividend:** NONE for FY26 — capital prioritized to growth (Jean Dousset retail capex) and debt repayment. Dividend to commence only after reaching zero net debt.
- **Debt:** ~INR120 cr repaid in Q4; net debt ~INR200 cr; targeting zero net debt in ~2 years.
- **Buyback:** possible once at zero net debt ("company may buy back shares") — subject to Board, nothing committed.
- Mkt investments (~INR100 cr Indian + US equities) and Bhavnagar land still held (potential monetization optionality).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation (buybacks, dividends, debt)

bull_bear.body:
- **US consumer demand:** revenue heavily US-discretionary (lab-diamond engagement rings) — cyclically sensitive.
- **US tariffs:** US import tariff on jewellery is the structural risk for a US-importing exporter — NOT discussed/quantified this call (gap).
- **Customer / brand concentration:** growth thesis leans on Jean Dousset store roll-out executing at modeled economics.
- **Gold/diamond price:** managed via natural USD hedge + forwards.
- **De-rating / sentiment:** stock down ~35-50% over 16-18 months; multiple investor questions on price/dividend/buyback met with "no comment" — persistent valuation/sentiment overhang.
- Execution risk on simultaneous M&A + 4-store rollout + integration.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Confident, growth-focused, disciplined on capital (debt-down before dividends). Specific, quantified guidance (D2C INR375 cr FY27, INR1,000 cr FY29, 20-30% profit growth). Credible execution track record (acquisitions grown 3-5x). Candid on inability/refusal to comment on share price ("I have no comments on that"), which read as honest but left aggrieved retail holders unsatisfied. Overall: operationally credible, capital-allocation disciplined, transparent on what they can/can't control.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The blended group still looks like a single-digit-EBITDA-margin exporter (~8%), masking a 12.6%-and-rising US D2C engine — re-rating hinges on D2C mix crossing over.
- Per-store economics are unusually rich: ~INR30-35 cr sales and ~INR8-10 cr PBT per Jean Dousset store implies ~25-30% store-level PBT margin — 4 new stores could add meaningful EPS if achieved.
- With Clarity 5x-in-4-years is the proof-point for the "buy undervalued D2C brand, scale it" playbook now reapplied to Jean Dousset.
- Natural USD cost-hedge (gold/diamonds bought in USD) materially de-risks FX vs typical exporters.
- Heavy retail-shareholder frustration on a ~35-50% drawdown + no dividend; management explicitly ties dividend/buyback to hitting zero net debt (~2 yrs) — a catalyst clock.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Received the 51st India Gem & Jewellery Awards - IGJA 2025-26 for being the country's largest exporter of silver jewellery for the year 2025-26
- Ethical and responsible sourcing: primarily engages Responsible Jewellery Council (RJC) audited vendors, with every supplier put through Know Your Supplier (KYS) due diligence
- In-house quality control: regular audits by the Quality Check department across the manufacturing process, plus product testing and quality assurance before market release
- Multi-geography subsidiary network spanning the USA, Dubai and India, with eleven subsidiaries (six direct and five step-down) as on the signing date of the Directors' Report
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Product quality — BRSR material-issue table: compromising on product quality poses serious risks to customer satisfaction and may result in product recalls, liability issues and reputational damage. Mitigated through a complaint-reporting mechanism, regular Quality Check department audits across the manufacturing process, and product testing before market release. The Company reports no negative financial impact during FY2025-26.
- Operational safety in manufacturing — BRSR material-issue table: manufacturing operations involve employee interaction with plant machinery and material handling equipment, which inherently carry risk of injury. Managed through safety protocols for hazardous materials and equipment, continuous risk assessments, corrective and preventive measures, and an annual HSE Report prepared by the HSE Committee for Senior Management review.
- Environmental impacts in the supply chain / raw-material dependence — BRSR material-issue table: the Company relies heavily on raw materials such as metals and gemstones whose extraction and processing can cause habitat destruction, water pollution and carbon emissions; any disruption or depletion directly affects sourcing capability, supply-chain stability and costs. Use of hazardous chemicals in manufacturing adds regulatory non-compliance and reputational exposure. Mitigated by supplier screening and engagement and by tracking emissions, water consumption and waste generation.
- Legal and regulatory change across operating regions — BRSR material-issue table: regulatory change in the regions where the Company operates can significantly impact operations and financial performance, potentially through higher costs, increased taxation, operational restrictions or bans on certain activities. Managed through a governance framework based on a philosophy of 'zero tolerance to non-compliance', continuous monitoring of legal developments, regular assessments and compliance management systems overseen by senior management and the Board.
- Labour conditions in the supply chain — BRSR material-issue table: notable challenges in ensuring fair labour practices, including employee health and safety, fair compensation and prevention of child or forced labour, especially with suppliers in regions with lower labour protections. Addressed through the Renaissance Jewellery Code of Practices, the Know Your Supplier (KYS) assessment covering legal, ethical and labour standards, regular audits, training and supplier engagement.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- **US D2C (Consumer Brands):** core growth engine. Jean Dousset (luxury lab-grown diamond engagement rings, avg ticket ~INR8-9 lakh; Jean Dousset = great-grandson of Louis Cartier; positioned as "most premium luxury lab-diamond brand in the world"). With Clarity (grown ~5x from ~INR40 cr to ~INR200 cr over 4 yrs). Enchanted Disney Fine Jewelry (licensed D2C).
- **Licensing/B2B:** exclusive fine-jewellery licensee for Disney; legacy B2B jewellery export business (bulk of revenue, lower margin).
- **Geography:** US-centric (revenue mostly US/USD); India is manufacturing/back-end.

latest_quarter.body:
- ~INR40 cr FY26 cost savings from sourcing/manufacturing/org integration.
- Mix shift to D2C (12.6%, targeting 15-20%) is the margin lever vs lower-margin B2B.
- **Hedging:** natural hedge — gold and diamonds purchased in USD, offsetting USD revenues; INR exposure covered via forward contracts with banks → "more or less completely hedged" on currency.
- **US tariff:** not addressed on this call; remains the key un-discussed cost risk for US-imported jewellery.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics (gold/diamond pass-through, mix, US tariff)

latest_quarter.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this):** FY26 rev INR2,572 cr (+29-30%), EBITDA INR204 cr (+22.5%), adj PAT INR100 cr (+36%). US D2C INR275 cr (+44%), D2C EBITDA margin 12.6% (vs 11.3% FY25). Net debt cut to ~INR200 cr (INR120 cr repaid in Q4); WC sharply improved (debtor days 124→109, inventory days 169→122). Jean Dousset 2→6 stores plan (4 in FY27); guidance: US D2C →INR375 cr FY27, profit growth 20-30%, INR1,000 cr D2C by FY29 at 15-20% EBITDA margin. No FY26 dividend (capital to growth + deleveraging); buyback only post zero-net-debt (~2 yrs). Stock de-rated ~35-50%; mgmt no comment on price.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- **US D2C revenue:** organic growth 35-40% in FY27 → **INR375 cr by end-FY27** (from INR275 cr FY26).
- **Profit growth:** **20-30% in FY27** (mgmt repeatedly: 25-30% annual profit growth for next 2-3 years), driven by rising D2C mix + efficiencies.
- **D2C ambition:** build a **INR1,000 cr D2C brand by FY29**, at **15-20% EBITDA margins**, via Jean Dousset expansion + other brands + digital + selective acquisitions.
- **Margin:** D2C EBITDA margin guided 15-20% (vs 12.6% blended US D2C now); group margin to lift as D2C mix rises.
- **US tariff:** NOT discussed on this call — no explicit tariff impact quantified (watch-item).
- **Capex:** funding 4 new Jean Dousset stores in FY27 (retail store build-out) — a stated reason for withholding dividend.
- **Net debt:** target zero net debt in next 12-24 months (~2 years).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)

outlook.body:
- Jean Dousset: **2 stores → 6 stores** by end-FY27 (4 new in FY27 across major US metropolitan luxury markets); 2nd NY store opened Nov-2025. Each store ~INR30-35 cr annual sales; ~INR8-10 cr to bottom line per store.
- Licensed brands (Disney): shift from channel-partner retail toward D2C via "Enchanted Disney Fine Jewelry" website, seeing 30-40% organic growth in that channel; FY27 priority to "fully capitalize on licensed brands via omnichannel."
- Inorganic pipeline: actively evaluating D2C/branded acquisitions (undervalued brands they can grow); nothing specific identified/named yet.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline (retail-partner programs, new brands)

outlook.body:
- Lab-grown diamond D2C is the flagship optionality (Jean Dousset luxury + With Clarity value).
- Disney-licensed D2C (Enchanted Disney) scaling via omnichannel.
- M&A optionality: track record of 3 acquisitions (Jay Gems/Disney licensee, With Clarity 2022, Jean Dousset 2025), each grown 3x-5x; continues to hunt undervalued D2C brands.
- INR1,000 cr D2C-by-FY29 platform ambition + selective bolt-ons.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality (D2C, lab-grown diamonds, new brand licences)

outlook.body:
- Expansion of Jean Dousset retail stores
- Pursuit of potential acquisition opportunities
- Reduction of debt levels
- Retention of earnings for the above: no equity dividend recommended and no amount transferred to General Reserve for FY2025-26
- Build-out of the Middle East presence: Verigold Jewellery FZCO established Renaissance Jewellery Middle East FZCO, Dubai as its wholly owned subsidiary and a step-down subsidiary of the Company during the year
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Annual Report contains no capacity-addition or plant-commissioning narrative. The only expansion intent stated is corporate and retail: the Board withheld a dividend for FY2025-26 in view of the Company's strategic focus on expansion of Jean Dousset retail stores, potential acquisition opportunities and reducing its debt levels. On the entity side, during the year M/s Verigold Jewellery FZCO, a subsidiary of RGL, established Renaissance Jewellery Middle East FZCO, Dubai as its wholly owned subsidiary and a step-down subsidiary of the Company, taking the group to eleven subsidiaries (six direct and five step-down) as on the signing date of the Directors' Report. No project timelines, capacities or rupee quantum are disclosed.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

deepdive.thesis: RGL is mid-transformation from a low-margin B2B jewellery exporter into a US-focused branded D2C platform (Jean Dousset luxury lab-diamond rings + With Clarity + Disney-licensed jewellery); FY26 delivered 29-30% revenue growth, ~22% EBITDA growth and 36% adjusted PAT growth with sharp debt + working-capital reduction, while management guides to a INR1,000cr D2C brand by FY29 and 20-30% annual profit growth — but the stock has de-rated ~35-50% and management has no answer for the price.

currentContext.expansion: The Annual Report contains no capacity-addition or plant-commissioning narrative. The only expansion intent stated is corporate and retail: the Board withheld a dividend for FY2025-26 in view of the Company's strategic focus on expansion of Jean Dousset retail stores, potential acquisition opportunities and reducing its debt levels. On the entity side, during the year M/s Verigold Jewellery FZCO, a subsidiary of RGL, established Renaissance Jewellery Middle East FZCO, Dubai as its wholly owned subsidiary and a step-down subsidiary of the Company, taking the group to eleven subsidiaries (six direct and five step-down) as on the signing date of the Directors' Report. No project timelines, capacities or rupee quantum are disclosed.

risks.note: BRSR material-issue table: compromising on product quality poses serious risks to customer satisfaction and may result in product recalls, liability issues and reputational damage. Mitigated through a complaint-reporting mechanism, regular Quality Check department audits across the manufacturing process, and product testing before market release. The Company reports no negative financial impact during FY2025-26.

BRSR material-issue table: manufacturing operations involve employee interaction with plant machinery and material handling equipment, which inherently carry risk of injury. Managed through safety protocols for hazardous materials and equipment, continuous risk assessments, corrective and preventive measures, and an annual HSE Report prepared by the HSE Committee for Senior Management review.

risks.risk: Environmental impacts in the supply chain / raw-material dependence
risks.note: BRSR material-issue table: the Company relies heavily on raw materials such as metals and gemstones whose extraction and processing can cause habitat destruction, water pollution and carbon emissions; any disruption or depletion directly affects sourcing capability, supply-chain stability and costs. Use of hazardous chemicals in manufacturing adds regulatory non-compliance and reputational exposure. Mitigated by supplier screening and engagement and by tracking emissions, water consumption and waste generation.

risks.risk: Legal and regulatory change across operating regions
risks.note: BRSR material-issue table: regulatory change in the regions where the Company operates can significantly impact operations and financial performance, potentially through higher costs, increased taxation, operational restrictions or bans on certain activities. Managed through a governance framework based on a philosophy of 'zero tolerance to non-compliance', continuous monitoring of legal developments, regular assessments and compliance management systems overseen by senior management and the Board.

risks.risk: Labour conditions in the supply chain
risks.note: BRSR material-issue table: notable challenges in ensuring fair labour practices, including employee health and safety, fair compensation and prevention of child or forced labour, especially with suppliers in regions with lower labour protections. Addressed through the Renaissance Jewellery Code of Practices, the Know Your Supplier (KYS) assessment covering legal, ethical and labour standards, regular audits, training and supplier engagement.

one-line thesis: RGL is mid-transformation from a low-margin B2B jewellery exporter into a US-focused branded D2C platform (Jean Dousset luxury lab-diamond rings + With Clarity + Disney-licensed jewellery); FY26 delivered 29-30% revenue growth, ~22% EBITDA growth and 36% adjusted PAT growth with sharp debt + working-capital reduction, while management guides to a INR1,000cr D2C brand by FY29 and 20-30% annual profit growth — but the stock has de-rated ~35-50% and management has no answer for the price.
financial scorecard:
**FY26 (full year):**
- **Revenue:** INR2,572 cr, +29-30% YoY. Growth led by US D2C / Consumer Brands segment.
- **EBITDA:** INR204 cr, +22-22.5% YoY (margin ~7.9% on reported revenue; mix still B2B-heavy).
- **PBT before exceptional items:** INR124 cr, +45% YoY.
- **Adjusted PAT (before exceptionals):** INR100 cr, +36% YoY.
- **US D2C revenue:** INR275 cr, +44% YoY (Jean Dousset + other brands). **US D2C EBITDA margin: 12.6% (FY26) vs 11.3% (FY25)** — structurally higher-margin than B2B.

**Q4 FY26:**
- **Revenue (before bullion sales):** INR686 cr, +33% YoY.
- **EBITDA:** INR57 cr, +40% YoY (margin ~8.3%).
- **PBT before exceptional items:** INR36.5 cr, +83% YoY.

**Balance sheet / cash:**
- Gross debt reduced by ~INR120-123 cr in Q4 FY26 alone.
- Total debt ~INR450 cr; cash ~INR100 cr + investments ~INR100 cr (mkt investments still held, not sold) → **net debt ~INR200 cr** (mgmt: INR200-250 cr).
- Equity / capital ~INR1,550 cr → net debt/equity ~0.13-0.15x ("0.15-0.2").
- **One-offs / FX:** ~INR40 cr annual cost savings (sourcing, manufacturing efficiencies, org integration), realized while integrating Jean Dousset. Note: PAT figures quoted "before exceptional items" — exceptionals not quantified on call. Bhavnagar land not yet sold. Indian + US stock-market investments still on books.

**Branded mix / US exposure:** US D2C INR275 cr ≈ ~11% of FY26 revenue but the higher-margin, low-working-capital growth engine; balance is legacy B2B jewellery exports.
guidance (critical):
- **US D2C revenue:** organic growth 35-40% in FY27 → **INR375 cr by end-FY27** (from INR275 cr FY26).
- **Profit growth:** **20-30% in FY27** (mgmt repeatedly: 25-30% annual profit growth for next 2-3 years), driven by rising D2C mix + efficiencies.
- **D2C ambition:** build a **INR1,000 cr D2C brand by FY29**, at **15-20% EBITDA margins**, via Jean Dousset expansion + other brands + digital + selective acquisitions.
- **Margin:** D2C EBITDA margin guided 15-20% (vs 12.6% blended US D2C now); group margin to lift as D2C mix rises.
- **US tariff:** NOT discussed on this call — no explicit tariff impact quantified (watch-item).
- **Capex:** funding 4 new Jean Dousset stores in FY27 (retail store build-out) — a stated reason for withholding dividend.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Renaissance Global Limited is a jewellery manufacturer recognised as the country's largest exporter of silver jewellery for 2025-26.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures jewellery and relies heavily on raw materials such as metals and gemstones. Its manufacturing operations involve employee interaction with plant machinery and material handling equipment, with a Quality Check department conducting regular audits through the manufacturing process and product testing before goods reach the market. The business is run through a group of direct and step-down subsidiaries in the USA, Dubai and India, including a Jean Dousset retail store business whose expansion is a stated Board priority.

- **US D2C revenue:** organic growth 35-40% in FY27 → **INR375 cr by end-FY27** (from INR275 cr FY26).
- **Profit growth:** **20-30% in FY27** (mgmt repeatedly: 25-30% annual profit growth for next 2-3 years), driven by rising D2C mix + efficiencies.
- **D2C ambition:** build a **INR1,000 cr D2C brand by FY29**, at **15-20% EBITDA margins**, via Jean Dousset expansion + other brands + digital + selective acquisitions.
- **Margin:** D2C EBITDA margin guided 15-20% (vs 12.6% blended US D2C now); group margin to lift as D2C mix rises.
- **US tariff:** NOT discussed on this call — no explicit tariff impact quantified (watch-item).
- **Capex:** funding 4 new Jean Dousset stores in FY27 (retail store build-out) — a stated reason for withholding dividend.
- **Net debt:** target zero net debt in next 12-24 months (~2 years).
order book & pipeline (retail-partner pr:
- Jean Dousset: **2 stores → 6 stores** by end-FY27 (4 new in FY27 across major US metropolitan luxury markets); 2nd NY store opened Nov-2025. Each store ~INR30-35 cr annual sales; ~INR8-10 cr to bottom line per store.
- Licensed brands (Disney): shift from channel-partner retail toward D2C via "Enchanted Disney Fine Jewelry" website, seeing 30-40% organic growth in that channel; FY27 priority to "fully capitalize on licensed brands via omnichannel."
- Inorganic pipeline: actively evaluating D2C/branded acquisitions (undervalued brands they can grow); nothing specific identified/named yet.
segment / subsidiary detail (branded vs:
- **US D2C (Consumer Brands):** core growth engine. Jean Dousset (luxury lab-grown diamond engagement rings, avg ticket ~INR8-9 lakh; Jean Dousset = great-grandson of Louis Cartier; positioned as "most premium luxury lab-diamond brand in the world"). With Clarity (grown ~5x from ~INR40 cr to ~INR200 cr over 4 yrs). Enchanted Disney Fine Jewelry (licensed D2C).
- **Licensing/B2B:** exclusive fine-jewellery licensee for Disney; legacy B2B jewellery export business (bulk of revenue, lower margin).
- **Geography:** US-centric (revenue mostly US/USD); India is manufacturing/back-end.
growth verticals / optionality (d2c, lab:
- Lab-grown diamond D2C is the flagship optionality (Jean Dousset luxury + With Clarity value).
- Disney-licensed D2C (Enchanted Disney) scaling via omnichannel.
- M&A optionality: track record of 3 acquisitions (Jay Gems/Disney licensee, With Clarity 2022, Jean Dousset 2025), each grown 3x-5x; continues to hunt undervalued D2C brands.

margins & cost dynamics (gold/diamond pa:
- ~INR40 cr FY26 cost savings from sourcing/manufacturing/org integration.
- Mix shift to D2C (12.6%, targeting 15-20%) is the margin lever vs lower-margin B2B.
- **Hedging:** natural hedge — gold and diamonds purchased in USD, offsetting USD revenues; INR exposure covered via forward contracts with banks → "more or less completely hedged" on currency.
- **US tariff:** not addressed on this call; remains the key un-discussed cost risk for US-imported jewellery.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): - 4 new Jean Dousset US stores in FY27 (→6 total by end-FY27); each ~INR30-35 cr revenue / ~INR8-10 cr PBT contribution. Capex self-funded; cited as reason to defer dividend. Watch for store-rollout slippage and per-store economics holding at the existing-store run-rate.
capital allocation (buybacks, dividends,:
- **Dividend:** NONE for FY26 — capital prioritized to growth (Jean Dousset retail capex) and debt repayment. Dividend to commence only after reaching zero net debt.
- **Debt:** ~INR120 cr repaid in Q4; net debt ~INR200 cr; targeting zero net debt in ~2 years.
- **Buyback:** possible once at zero net debt ("company may buy back shares") — subject to Board, nothing committed.
- Mkt investments (~INR100 cr Indian + US equities) and Bhavnagar land still held (potential monetization optionality).
risks & watch-items:
- **US consumer demand:** revenue heavily US-discretionary (lab-diamond engagement rings) — cyclically sensitive.
- **US tariffs:** US import tariff on jewellery is the structural risk for a US-importing exporter — NOT discussed/quantified this call (gap).
- **Customer / brand concentration:** growth thesis leans on Jean Dousset store roll-out executing at modeled economics.
- **Gold/diamond price:** managed via natural USD hedge + forwards.
- **De-rating / sentiment:** stock down ~35-50% over 16-18 months; multiple investor questions on price/dividend/buyback met with "no comment" — persistent valuation/sentiment overhang.
- Execution risk on simultaneous M&A + 4-store rollout + integration.
management quality / tone: - Confident, growth-focused, disciplined on capital (debt-down before dividends). Specific, quantified guidance (D2C INR375 cr FY27, INR1,000 cr FY29, 20-30% profit growth). Credible execution track record (acquisitions grown 3-5x). Candid on inability/refusal to comment on share price ("I have no comments on that"), which read as honest but left aggrieved retail holders unsatisfied. Overall: operationally credible, capital-allocation disciplined, transparent on what they can/can't control.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The blended group still looks like a single-digit-EBITDA-margin exporter (~8%), masking a 12.6%-and-rising US D2C engine — re-rating hinges on D2C mix crossing over.
- Per-store economics are unusually rich: ~INR30-35 cr sales and ~INR8-10 cr PBT per Jean Dousset store implies ~25-30% store-level PBT margin — 4 new stores could add meaningful EPS if achieved.
- With Clarity 5x-in-4-years is the proof-point for the "buy undervalued D2C brand, scale it" playbook now reapplied to Jean Dousset.
- Natural USD cost-hedge (gold/diamonds bought in USD) materially de-risks FX vs typical exporters.
- Heavy retail-shareholder frustration on a ~35-50% drawdown + no dividend; management explicitly ties dividend/buyback to hitting zero net debt (~2 yrs) — a catalyst clock.
